title: Coding Agent vs Chatbot: 1 Loop, 4 Steps
description:
What is a coding agent, and how is it different from an AI chatbot? Learn how AI coding agents work in 60 seconds.
A chatbot only gives you text to paste and run yourself; a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot agent mode) reads your files, edits the code, runs commands and checks the result, in a loop until the job is done.

Try it: Claude Code https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works , Codex CLI https://github.com/openai/codex , or agent mode in VS Code.

Chapters
0:00 Why You Keep Pasting Code
0:20 What a Coding Agent Does
0:32 One Loop, Four Steps
0:44 You Stop Being the Messenger

The story: a mechanic on the phone can only talk, so you paste his fix, run it, and carry the error back to him. The same mechanic in your garage, with tools, reads the engine, turns the bolt, starts it and listens, and goes around again until the job is done. That is the difference between a chatbot and a coding agent: one agent, one loop, four steps (read, edit, run, check). The whole visit, every step and every result, is one session. You stop being the messenger: you watch, and you can stop it at any moment.

The takeaway: the model didn't get a bigger brain. It got hands (tools), and a way to check its own work. It can still be wrong, so give it a test to run.

"4 steps" is this video's simple drawing of the loop. Anthropic describes the agentic loop as gather context, take action, verify results; the makers' own words for the tools are read your code, edit files, run commands. Before chatbots and agents there was autocomplete: the first GitHub Copilot (2021) suggested whole lines as you typed.
